An analysis of the Kepler Objects of Interest (KOI) dataset shows that all of the listed columns represent properties of the star (such as `ra`, `dec`, `koi_steff`, `koi_slogg`, `koi_srad`, `koi_kepmag`), properties of the transit event detected by the Kepler pipeline (such as `koi_period`, `koi_time0bk`, `koi_impact`, `koi_duration`, `koi_depth`, `koi_prad`, `koi_teq`, `koi_insol`, `koi_model_snr`), their associated measurement uncertainties, or automated vetting flags (`koi_fpflag_nt`, `koi_fpflag_ss`, `koi_fpflag_co`, `koi_fpflag_ec`). 

All of these values are calculated and finalized during the initial automated pipeline processing and vetting of the Threshold Crossing Event (TCE) before a final disposition (`koi_disposition`) is assigned. Therefore, all of these columns are `AVAILABLE` at the moment of prediction.
